## Strategy guide

This is a strategy guide, not a current-rules ruling. It reflects SCPT 302 (2023-06-07) and the supplied complete ASR transcript; expansion and ruleset compatibility remain unreviewed. The transcript contains recognition errors, and the speakers revise views or disagree. Treat rules-sensitive readings as episode interpretations. Captured plastic is not trade goods, preparation is not scoring, and an action-phase stall is not a formal pass.

Cabal trades ordinary trade-good income for reach, production and captured units. Its visible threat can isolate it; durable board presence still offers no dependable route to the tenth point.

Construction is the usual round-one choice for the second dock. Leadership can outrank it when tokens constrain builds and movement; Trade or Diplomacy can substitute when their likely proceeds support production. Vortex is the usual early technology when nearby targets are worthwhile. These are defaults conditioned by slice, map, objectives and table response.

### Claims

#### C03

Devour captures enemy non-structure units destroyed during combat. Captured pieces go to Cabal’s sheet and feed faction abilities; captured fighters and infantry do not remove the opponent’s plastic. **Apply when:** Captured pieces are separate from trade goods and do not themselves remove opponent pieces. **Limit:** Current rules and edge cases are unchecked. **Evidence:** 16:08.60–16:14.24 (s000344); 16:37.14–16:42.26 (s000349); 17:11.52–17:17.88 (s000356); 17:28.22–17:33.62 (s000359).

#### C04

In the hosts’ blockade explanation, enemy ships above a Cabal dock with no Cabal ships blockade that dock. Cabal ships entering end that local blockade; while an opponent maintains it, that player gets their captured units back and Cabal cannot capture that blocker’s units. **Apply when:** Treat this as the episode’s rules interpretation: a blockade is local to the dock system, and the blocker must remain in the defined state. **Limit:** The speakers call the interaction rulesy; verify the current rule text before relying on it. **Evidence:** 18:47.46–18:52.24 (s000384); 18:52.24–18:55.52 (s000385); 19:31.64–19:35.14 (s000398); 19:35.38–19:37.02 (s000399); 19:37.54–19:39.24 (s000400); 19:39.68–19:42.60 (s000401); 19:43.06–19:44.88 (s000402); 20:00.00–20:04.74 (s000406); 20:04.74–20:07.82 (s000407); 20:08.66–20:13.36 (s000408); 20:13.36–20:17.60 (s000409); 20:17.86–20:21.08 (s000410); 20:21.08–20:26.08 (s000411); 20:26.08–20:33.08 (s000412); 20:33.08–20:38.64 (s000413).

#### C05

Amalgamation converts a matching captured unit into production without spending resources; Riftmeld consumes a matching captured unit to skip upgrade prerequisites. Technology still costs resources, so the abilities compete for captured plastic. **Apply when:** Choose the use that best serves the current build or research need. **Limit:** Wording and costs are not checked against current text. **Evidence:** 17:33.62–17:36.82 (s000360); 17:36.82–17:42.48 (s000361); 17:47.28–17:51.68 (s000363); 17:51.68–17:56.74 (s000364); 17:56.74–18:02.72 (s000365); 18:02.72–18:06.78 (s000366).

#### C06

A Dimensional Tear creates a gravity rift, gives Cabal ships special exit movement, stores up to six fighters outside capacity and has flat production five in the hosts’ description. Its location shapes both movement and builds. **Apply when:** Stored fighters are not general fleet capacity; value depends on dock placement. **Limit:** Component description is not an independent rules check. **Evidence:** 20:51.78–20:57.42 (s000418); 20:57.42–21:00.36 (s000419); 21:00.36–21:06.58 (s000420); 21:07.10–21:11.94 (s000421); 21:12.65–21:13.70 (s000422); 21:21.64–21:26.52 (s000425); 21:26.52–21:32.56 (s000426).

#### C08

The Terror Between captures non-structure units destroyed in its system, including Cabal’s own losses; its bombardment can capture too. It can refill plastic after a large fight, but cannot capture itself when it dies. **Apply when:** Its payoff depends on combat losses in its system. **Limit:** The hosts’ tier rating is opinion. **Evidence:** 23:32.56–23:37.72 (s000473); 23:37.72–23:40.22 (s000474); 24:12.26–24:16.96 (s000488); 24:16.96–24:20.64 (s000489); 25:17.38–25:20.64 (s000514); 25:20.82–25:22.38 (s000515).

#### C10

After another player replenishes commodities, the agent can exhaust to convert available commodities into trade goods and capture one unit costing no more than that player’s commodity value. The hosts say a Trade Agreement taking the commodities first does not prevent the capture. **Apply when:** The captured unit’s cost is limited by commodity value; the speakers describe the Trade Agreement timing as an after-step interaction. **Limit:** The hosts’ timing explanation is not checked against a current FAQ. **Evidence:** 29:43.61–29:47.77 (s000595); 29:47.77–29:54.97 (s000596); 29:54.97–29:59.87 (s000597); 30:00.00–30:29.98 (s000598); 30:29.98–30:34.32 (s000599); 30:34.32–30:38.48 (s000600); 30:38.48–30:41.78 (s000601); 30:41.78–30:45.62 (s000602).

#### C11

The commander unlocks with Cabal units in three gravity rifts; the hosts count each Dimensional Tear as one. Its bonus lets up to two fighters or infantry exceed production limits, but Cabal still pays for them. **Apply when:** Use when resources and unit needs justify it; extra capacity is not free plastic. **Limit:** Unlock examples are episode explanations, not rules verification. **Evidence:** 33:35.48–33:37.94 (s000674); 33:37.94–33:39.72 (s000675); 33:39.72–33:41.42 (s000676); 34:01.50–34:04.82 (s000690); 34:04.82–34:07.52 (s000691); 34:07.52–34:10.82 (s000692); 34:10.82–34:12.64 (s000693).

#### C12

The hero is an action that randomly captures eligible units around Dimensional Tears. The hosts call it unreliable but recommend using it as a stall when delay matters; late captures may arrive too late to spend. Treat it as an action-phase stall, not as if you had formally passed. **Apply when:** Use it when waiting has value and targets are in or adjacent to a Tear; do not plan around a high roll. **Limit:** The rules timing follows the hosts’ action description; impact is anecdotal. **Evidence:** 35:57.64–36:00.44 (s000729); 36:00.88–36:04.56 (s000730); 36:04.56–36:06.56 (s000731); 36:06.70–36:08.26 (s000732); 36:08.26–36:11.18 (s000733); 36:11.18–36:16.36 (s000734); 36:53.48–36:55.26 (s000750); 37:11.66–37:14.48 (s000758); 37:24.24–37:26.30 (s000763); 37:26.30–37:27.64 (s000764); 37:27.72–37:29.60 (s000765).

#### C13

Construction is the hosts’ near-automatic round-one pick because Cabal wants its second dock and fears the table may avoid taking the card. Passing needs an unusually strong slice-specific reason. **Apply when:** Assumes the card is available; the map or objective can change the pick. **Limit:** Strong podcast advice, not a tested universal order. **Evidence:** 51:06.06–51:07.80 (s001034); 51:07.98–51:08.88 (s001035); 51:28.96–51:35.76 (s001046); 51:36.52–51:43.14 (s001047); 51:43.14–51:48.84 (s001048); 51:48.84–51:54.24 (s001049).

#### C14

Leadership supports repeated activations and builds. Cabal should spend planets before round end and turn captured plastic into board presence; its high command-token demand can constrain that plan. **Apply when:** Favor tokens when builds and movement compete, especially with resource-heavy, low-influence slices. **Limit:** Token needs are experiential. **Evidence:** 53:00.58–53:03.62 (s001072); 53:03.62–53:08.28 (s001073); 53:42.52–53:46.44 (s001080); 53:46.44–53:52.80 (s001081); 53:52.80–53:53.20 (s001082); 54:05.58–54:08.34 (s001087); 54:08.62–54:12.80 (s001088); 54:12.80–54:13.24 (s001089); 85:40.74–85:45.24 (s001671); 85:45.24–85:47.32 (s001672).

#### C15

The hosts compare Trade and Diplomacy as ways to fund plastic. Diplomacy can turn Cabal’s four-resource home into a build; compare the likely proceeds from Diplomacy with Trade rather than assuming either pays more. **Apply when:** Actual value depends on map, timing and table. **Limit:** The episode does not settle a fixed ranking. **Evidence:** 55:13.32–55:17.80 (s001113); 55:17.80–55:22.50 (s001114); 55:22.50–55:24.42 (s001115); 55:35.46–55:37.96 (s001118); 55:37.96–55:45.04 (s001119); 55:45.76–55:53.04 (s001120); 58:29.20–58:33.68 (s001167); 58:34.34–58:38.70 (s001168); 58:38.70–58:43.22 (s001169).

#### C18

Do not delay the third dock while seeking a perfect site. It opens Vortex and hero targets, broadens movement and creates more build options; adjacency to useful systems matters most. **Apply when:** Place to expand reach and objective options; exact placement is map-dependent. **Limit:** The guide rejects one universal location. **Evidence:** 61:29.28–61:31.04 (s001215); 83:07.04–83:09.24 (s001622); 83:23.76–83:27.80 (s001629).

#### C19

Vortex is the usual early technology because it captures a unit from reinforcements adjacent to a dock without winning combat. Delay it if nearby targets are low value and another upgrade better serves the opening. **Apply when:** Research early when a worthwhile target improves the build plan. **Limit:** Target value is board-specific; ranking is opinion. **Evidence:** 38:57.72–39:01.64 (s000791); 39:06.48–39:13.18 (s000793); 39:43.62–39:47.42 (s000801).

#### C20

Carrier II plus Fighter II is the guide’s core upgrade package: carriers extend reach and the hosts call the pair Cabal’s bread and butter. This is a practical mainline after Vortex, not a universal requirement. **Apply when:** Favor it when reach matters and Cabal can support fleets with fighters, infantry and tokens. **Limit:** Preference depends on skips, captures and objectives. **Evidence:** 63:25.98–63:30.84 (s001254); 63:30.84–63:36.50 (s001255); 63:36.50–63:40.16 (s001256); 63:40.16–63:43.56 (s001257); 63:43.88–63:47.02 (s001258); 63:47.02–63:47.52 (s001259); 63:47.98–63:50.44 (s001260); 63:51.10–63:52.82 (s001261).

#### C21

Avoid spending every capture on dreadnoughts. Mixing carriers and dreads keeps carriers available for Cabal’s plans, while captured carriers can deny opponents a unit they may need. **Apply when:** Choose around transport, capacity and the next objective. **Limit:** No fixed ratio is recommended. **Evidence:** 40:52.80–40:58.10 (s000821); 40:58.10–41:04.24 (s000822); 41:04.76–41:08.76 (s000823); 41:08.76–41:14.30 (s000824); 41:14.30–41:19.54 (s000825).

#### C25

The commander’s Alliance has a time-sensitive sale window: factions may value extra fighter or infantry production, but value falls when Cabal delays the unlock. The hosts describe it as worth roughly one or two trade goods to a buyer who needs the capacity. **Apply when:** Unlock early enough for a buyer to use it; price against remaining rounds and actual need. **Limit:** Buyer interest and price are anecdotal. **Evidence:** 69:34.24–69:39.38 (s001363); 69:39.48–69:41.84 (s001364); 70:00.00–70:04.06 (s001369); 70:04.14–70:11.74 (s001370); 70:11.74–70:16.82 (s001371); 70:21.94–70:26.16 (s001373); 70:26.16–70:30.82 (s001374); 70:30.82–70:36.02 (s001375).

#### C26

Crucible can be traded for payment or favors, and its movement can help an ally reach a useful rift route. The hosts frame a promissory note’s best trade as one that helps the buyer score. **Apply when:** Seek payment when it mainly enables another player’s point; shared tactics may justify a favor. **Limit:** The examples are situational and do not guarantee a price. **Evidence:** 71:47.92–71:50.44 (s001399); 71:50.44–71:54.26 (s001400); 73:01.00–73:03.40 (s001426); 73:03.40–73:06.56 (s001427); 73:06.56–73:08.54 (s001428); 74:11.64–74:17.30 (s001445); 74:17.30–74:24.84 (s001446).

#### C27

The speakers preserve two negotiating styles: one sees the fleet as a credible threat; another prefers small asks that accumulate value without uniting the table. Bargain around real timing or access instead of assuming intimidation earns support. **Apply when:** Set a proportionate ask against benefit; aggression can cost cooperation Cabal lacks. **Limit:** The hosts openly differ on threatening and fighting. **Evidence:** 78:14.14–78:18.98 (s001521); 79:43.82–79:47.02 (s001550); 81:01.54–81:06.62 (s001577); 81:51.36–81:53.44 (s001595).

#### C28

Cabal’s early budget leans toward plastic: the hosts describe using the four-resource home for units and say they make few trade goods. They also stress command-token demand and value a high-influence slice. **Apply when:** Use influence and tokens deliberately; account for the revealed objective’s actual requirement. **Limit:** This economic comparison is experiential, not measured. **Evidence:** 53:46.44–53:52.80 (s001081); 53:52.80–53:53.20 (s001082); 54:05.58–54:08.34 (s001087); 54:08.62–54:12.80 (s001088); 54:12.80–54:13.24 (s001089); 55:13.32–55:17.80 (s001113); 55:17.80–55:22.50 (s001114); 55:22.50–55:24.42 (s001115).

#### C30

Cabal can prepare for stage-one control and upgrade objectives through movement, docks and captured units, but preparation is not a point until the requirement is met. Ground control needs more planning than fleets in empty space. **Apply when:** Match units and timing to the objective; do not count likely access as scoring. **Limit:** Broad advice, not a claim every stage one is easy. **Evidence:** 90:51.32–90:56.62 (s001779); 91:08.00–91:15.94 (s001782); 91:26.30–91:29.74 (s001785).

#### C31

Cabal can be hard to remove once spread across the board, but the hosts say finding the 10th point is difficult and stage twos can be harder; they identify no reliable late-game closer. **Apply when:** Keep a route to bonus points or stage twos, adapting to revealed objectives; extra plastic does not force a win. **Limit:** Tournament review is selective and anecdotal; no repeatable Cabal line is claimed. **Evidence:** 91:57.64–92:02.40 (s001793); 93:24.34–93:29.32 (s001823); 94:48.58–94:49.34 (s001851); 97:56.24–97:59.06 (s001909); 99:44.72–99:49.30 (s001953).

#### C32

Target access is a Cabal constraint: Vortex selects an opponent’s non-structure unit adjacent to a Dimensional Tear and captures a matching unit from their reinforcements, while the hero checks units in or adjacent to a Tear. The hosts note Vortex can be poor when opponents keep their units away. **Apply when:** Assess nearby targets and dock placement before valuing either capture effect. **Limit:** The Vortex example is one game; target availability is map-dependent. **Evidence:** 35:57.64–36:00.44 (s000729); 36:00.88–36:04.56 (s000730); 36:04.56–36:06.56 (s000731); 36:06.70–36:08.26 (s000732); 36:08.26–36:11.18 (s000733); 36:11.18–36:16.36 (s000734); 38:53.20–38:57.72 (s000790); 38:57.72–39:01.64 (s000791); 39:01.64–39:06.48 (s000792); 39:34.78–39:37.96 (s000798).

#### C33

The guide does not settle whether Cabal should fight or wait: one host values force for unusual points, while another recounts success with good objectives and restraint. Read fleet projection as leverage, not an order to attack every neighbor. **Apply when:** Fight for points or useful captures when responses are manageable; otherwise economy and timing may preserve a route. **Limit:** This is an explicit disagreement shaped by different play styles. **Evidence:** 44:55.88–45:00.34 (s000900); 45:25.22–45:32.50 (s000906); 47:14.36–47:16.64 (s000951); 49:42.06–49:49.92 (s001012).

### Source limits

This is an episode-derived strategic interpretation, not a current rules reference. Retain the hosts’ disagreement and uncertainty; verify rules-sensitive interactions against the applicable rules and FAQ before relying on them. Capturing, producing, destroying, storing, and scoring are distinct events.

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Vuil&#x27;raith Cabal (`cabal`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-vuilraith-cabal-cabal) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-vuilraith-cabal-cabal)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Acheron 4/0; start 1 dreadnought, 1 carrier, 1 cruiser, 3 fighters, 3
infantry, Dimensional Tear dock (PRODUCTION 5; its system is a gravity rift the Cabal does not roll
for; 6 fighters free of capacity); starting tech Self-Assembly Routines; 2 commodities. Devour:
capture opponents' non-structure units destroyed in combat. Amalgamation: return a captured unit to
produce one of that type free. Riftmeld: return a captured unit to research its upgrade ignoring
prerequisites. Vortex (R): capture a unit from a player near your docks. Agent: after a player
replenishes commodities, convert them to trade goods and capture a unit costing up to their
commodity value. Commander (units in 3 gravity rifts).

**Opening.** Trade in round 1 and play it early, refreshing everyone (goodwill); when a
4-commodity player refreshes, the agent captures a dreadnought or carrier; Warfare's secondary for
two carriers; Construction early to put a Dimensional Tear near Mecatol Rex, lining docks up as
rift highways ([BGG "Any tips on how to play Vuil'Raith Cabal?", 2020-21](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2556786)).
Leadership matters: zero starting influence, token poor.

**Play.** Aggression is cheap for the Cabal (captures pay for losses), but do not unify the table
early; from round 3 on, fight a lot ([BGG "The Vuil'Raith Cabal", 2022](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2880251)).
Fleet supply caps how many free captured ships can be built. Use captured units with Riftmeld to
get upgrades. They struggle against PDS-heavy defences and tough infantry (Sol, Yin, Sardakk,
Mahact).

**Strength.** SCPT row 3 (2022), A (2025); async PoK B.

**Bot feasibility.**
- Production: Amalgamation prompts (free unit for a captured one) should always be taken. Value
  medium, effort S.
- Agent on commodity replenishment: always use, target the most expensive capturable unit.
  Effort S-M.
- Targeting: fights are cheaper for the Cabal (captures), so accept a slightly lower win margin
  (e.g. `WIN_MARGIN` 0.3). Value medium, effort S.
- Movement through own Dimensional Tears is already a gravity rift without a roll in the engine;
  check that `movable_into` counts the +1. Value low.
- Draft: Trade and Leadership up, Construction up in round 1. Effort S.

</details>

  II (YY), `vtx` Vortex (R). Flagship (combat 5) captures everything destroyed in its system.

- **Mid**: dreadnoughts and fighters into fights it can win. **Late**: flagship-led fleet.

  red.
- **Build**: mid dreadnoughts (3), fighters, carrier; late flagship, dreadnoughts (4).
- **Cards/tokens**: Warfare; a deep fleet pool.

The speakers call Vortex and the agent the faction’s actual economic power; Vortex is target-dependent, while the agent resolves after another player replenishes commodities. - [Dimensional Tear I](../components.md#unit-cabal-spacedock) **enables** [That Which Molds Flesh](../components.md#leader-cabalcommander). The commander unlock requires Cabal units in three gravity rifts, and each Dimensional Tear is a gravity rift. Sources: [SCPT 302, 2017.94–2019.72s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 2019.72–2021.42s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/)
- [Amalgamation](../components.md#ability-amalgamation) **conflicts-with** [Riftmeld](../components.md#ability-riftmeld). Both use a captured unit of the matching type: Amalgamation pays it to produce without resources, while Riftmeld returns it to ignore upgrade prerequisites; the technology still costs resources. Sources: [SCPT 302, 1053.62–1056.82s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1056.82–1062.48s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1067.28–1071.68s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1071.68–1076.74s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1076.74–1082.72s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1082.72–1086.78s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/)
- [Crucible](../components.md#promissory-crucible) **enables** [Dimensional Tear I](../components.md#unit-cabal-spacedock). Crucible’s movement bonus can combine with a Dimensional Tear’s gravity-rift movement to extend a route. Sources: [SCPT 302, 1624.30–1630.86s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1630.86–1637.08s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1637.08–1641.32s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1655.76–1660.46s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1660.46–1667.88s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1667.88–1672.80s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1677.92–1683.94s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 1683.94–1688.32s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/)
- [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction) **enables** [Dimensional Tear I](../components.md#unit-cabal-spacedock). Construction gives the early second dock the hosts call a need, and they recommend taking the card round one if available. Sources: [SCPT 302, 3066.06–3067.80s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 3067.98–3068.88s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 3088.96–3095.76s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 3096.52–3103.14s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 3103.14–3108.84s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/); [SCPT 302, 3108.84–3114.24s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/302-super-vuil-raith-cabal-guide/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Devour captures enemy non-structure units destroyed during combat. Captured pieces go to Cabal’s sheet and feed faction abilities; captured fighters and infantry do not remove the opponent’s plastic.
  Conditions: Captured pieces are separate from trade goods and do not themselves remove opponent pieces. Compatibility: SCPT 302 (2023-06-07); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Current rules and edge cases are unchecked.

- **Draft:** Avoid spending every capture on dreadnoughts. Mixing carriers and dreads keeps carriers available for Cabal’s plans, while captured carriers can deny opponents a unit they may need.

<a id="claim-c25"></a>

- **Draft:** The commander’s Alliance has a time-sensitive sale window: factions may value extra fighter or infantry production, but value falls when Cabal delays the unlock. The hosts describe it as worth roughly one or two trade goods to a buyer who needs the capacity.
  Conditions: Unlock early enough for a buyer to use it; price against remaining rounds and actual need. Compatibility: SCPT 302 (2023-06-07); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Buyer interest and price are anecdotal.

- **Draft:** Crucible can be traded for payment or favors, and its movement can help an ally reach a useful rift route. The hosts frame a promissory note’s best trade as one that helps the buyer score.
  Conditions: Seek payment when it mainly enables another player’s point; shared tactics may justify a favor. Compatibility: SCPT 302 (2023-06-07); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: The examples are situational and do not guarantee a price.

- **Draft:** The speakers preserve two negotiating styles: one sees the fleet as a credible threat; another prefers small asks that accumulate value without uniting the table. Bargain around real timing or access instead of assuming intimidation earns support.

- **Draft:** Cabal’s early budget leans toward plastic: the hosts describe using the four-resource home for units and say they make few trade goods. They also stress command-token demand and value a high-influence slice.
  Conditions: Use influence and tokens deliberately; account for the revealed objective’s actual requirement. Compatibility: SCPT 302 (2023-06-07); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: This economic comparison is experiential, not measured.

- **Draft:** Cabal can prepare for stage-one control and upgrade objectives through movement, docks and captured units, but preparation is not a point until the requirement is met. Ground control needs more planning than fleets in empty space.

- **Draft:** The guide does not settle whether Cabal should fight or wait: one host values force for unusual points, while another recounts success with good objectives and restraint. Read fleet projection as leverage, not an order to attack every neighbor.
